pr_title: Make the table name too long error message more explicit for Postgres
pr_body:
Fixes #49557

Makes it explicit why the enforced limit for max table name length is less than the default Postgres limit.
pr_comments: You'll need to update all the tests added in https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/45136. I also think maybe it's better to extract the error message out to its own method so that the check logic isn't duplicated between adapters.

Thanks @ghiculescu I've moved the error message out into its own method and fixed the tests.
Are you happy with the `if current_adapter?(:PostgreSQLAdapter)` statement in the tests?
Once the tests are green, could you [squash](https://guides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#squashing-commits) your commits please.

Thanks very much @yahonda and @ghiculescu 
I've made the changes and squashed the commits.
Let me know if there's anything else you think needs to happen.
Would it be possible to automatically shorten the table name? Similar to https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/47753
@p8 I don't think so -- index names are mostly unimportant after definition, whereas expectations and mentions of table names appear all over the place.
From memory the original issue was that dropping tables with long names doesn’t work because the index names matter then. I suppose we could fix that more directly?

> Does #49592 fix the issue?

Yes, that's a much better solution. I'll close this PR.

issue_context.title: The Postgres adapter's "table name too long" error message is confusing
issue_context.body:
The PR #45136 enforces a maximum table name length when creating tables.

The error message is:
`Table name '#{table_name}' is too long; the limit is #{table_name_length} characters`

The issue is `table_name_length` for Postgres returns 58 characters. All the Postgres docs show a max table length of 63 characters. The reason it's different is that we're reducing it by 5 characters to allow for `_pkey` suffix Postgres adds.

I encountered the error when upgrading an app to Rails 7.1 and it wasn't immediately obvious to me why my table name that was 60 characters long should be an issue.  I had to check the Rails source code to find out why it wasn't working.

My suggestion is to add something to the error message to save people having to dig through the Rails code to figure out why the max allowed by Rails is less than the max allowed by Postgres.

I'm happy to submit a PR if it's something the core team are happy to add.
comments: A PR to make an error message more useful is always 👍

review_comments:
We usually end errors with periods. I noticed this was like that before, but let's add one now.

```suggestion
          "Table name '#{table_name}' is too long; the limit is #{table_name_length} characters."
```
